Scene:
The Drowned Rat (drowned-rat) present=marla,tam,greely

Known canon:
[Sera Valen] Emberhollow's own: a cleric of the Dawnfather, back home for the first time in two years, summoned by Father Oswin's letter.
[Corvin] A peddler whose cart arrived the morning after the collapse. Sells oddments and trades in rumors; wears a miner's salt-charm though he's never swung a pick.
[Derva Saltbeard] Dwarf forewoman, missing in the mine. She warned Greely for a month that the east gallery was unsound and should stay sealed.
[Father Oswin] Priest of the Dawnfather who raised Sera Valen after her parents died of saltlung. Sent word asking her to come home the day after the collapse.
[Alderman Hobb Greely] Owns the mine and most of the town's debts. Nervous, generous with promises, slow with coin.
[Marla Fenwick] Keeps the Drowned Rat tavern. Missing two fingers on her left hand and tells a different story about it every time. Keeps the miners' corner mug filled until they come home.
[Tam] The only miner to escape the collapse. Swears he saw 'pale folk with wet mouths' in the dark before the roof came down. The town half-believes him.
[The collapse] Alderman Greely has posted a reward of 50 gold for anyone who brings the missing miners out, alive or dead.
[The collapse] Three days ago a section of the saltmine's east workings collapsed. Six miners are missing, including forewoman Derva Saltbeard.
[Emberhollow] A salt-mining town of about two hundred souls, three days from anywhere, built on the Greely Mineral Concern's saltmine.

(no events)

Narration:
Rain freckles the tavern windows and turns the front door black with damp. Inside, the Drowned Rat glows in stubborn little islands: the banked hearth breathing red, three candle stubs along Marla Fenwick’s counter, one nervous flame parked hard by Tam’s elbow. Marla drums her three-fingered hand on the wood and watches the room like it owes her money. In the corner, a full mug waits at the miners’ table, untouched, gathering no dust because someone keeps wiping the ring clean.

Father Oswin’s letter is still creased in your pocket: come home at once. The mine has fallen in. Derva Saltbeard is missing. Tam made it out babbling about pale folk in the dark, and now half the town calls him mad while the other half won’t go near the shaft after sunset.

Across from you, Alderman Greely mops his temples and forces a smile. “Mistress Valen. A mercy you’re here. We have a situation.” Tam’s candle gutters. Marla snorts through her nose.

Your moment.

“My dear Mistress Valen, a regrettable collapse, nothing more exotic than bad stone and worse luck.” He spreads his hands, but his thumb worries one cufflink so hard it nearly twists loose. “We are, ah, doing all that can be done.”

Marla gives a dry little laugh. “Hear that? Man’s rehearsed.” Greely’s jaw tightens. “Mind your trade, woman.”
